title: Short Stuff: 666
summary: Short Stuff episode on the number 666 (the number of the beast). The hosts discuss the Book of Revelation 13:18 verse, how it has been used in pop culture (The Omen), and the ancient Greek practice of isopsephy (assigning numeric values to letters) that makes 666 a code. They cover the leading interpretation that it encodes Nero (Caesar Nero transliterated into Hebrew, nrwnqsr, sums to 666), the objections to that reading (Revelation was written in Greek, and the beast not yet being born), and the alternative reading that 666 is a human number signaling Satan as a cheap imitation of God's seven. Light banter about Iron Maiden and a mention of a Dave Russell article on HowStuffWorks.

segments.title: Opening banter and Iron Maiden
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter about Iron Maiden and Bruce Dickinson, and a joke about a license plate reading 666.

segments.title: Revelation 13:18 and the number of the beast
segments.summary: The hosts read Revelation 13:18 and explain that the verse describes the number of the beast as 666. They note the number's pop culture use in The Omen, where Damien has 666 on his scalp.

segments.title: Isopsephy and Greek letter numbers
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Greek letters and Hebrew letters carried numeric values, so words and names could be summed. This practice, isopsephy, was a common word game in the first century CE.

segments.title: Nero as the beast
segments.summary: The hosts explain the leading interpretation that 666 encodes Nero. Nero equals 1005, matching the phrase 'his mother slew', and Caesar Nero transliterated into Hebrew (nrwnqsr) sums to 666.

segments.title: Objections and alternative interpretations
segments.summary: The hosts describe objections to the Nero reading: Revelation was written in Greek, the Hebrew step seems a stretch, and the beast was not yet born in Nero's time. They describe another reading in which 666 is a human number, making Satan a cheap imitation of God's seven.

segments.title: Wrap-up and Iron Maiden
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up by noting that the number is either Nero or a sign of Satan as a cheap imitation of God, and reference the 'Number of the Beast' Iron Maiden song.
topics: Iron Maiden Number of the Beast

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts sign off, pointing listeners to the HowStuffWorks article and the show's production credits.
